pages.text: With technology or flesh shrines, you can make $(bold)golems$() and $(bold)homunculi$() respectively. If a bound mob (not an idol) is in a diagram influencing the shrine, the shrine will attempt to spend spirits equal to thrice the mob's max HP to create a copy of the bound mob, which will behave as if bound but will not require bindings. Technology and flesh shrines will not drain spirits from mobs.
The copies will be retextured with the appropriate spirit type.

Golems and homunculi do not drop items, and will start taking frequent damage if they are not in the range of a shrine of their spirit type.$(br2)Golems have half the speed of their source mob, but overfilling a tech shrine will make all golems in range faster, and with enough spirits you can more than compensate. The same applies to homunculi and attack strength.

3 spirits per minute will double a golem's speed (returning it to normal), 9 will triple it, 27 will quadruple it, and so on. 3 spirits per minute will add an extra 3 damage to a homunculus attack, 9 will add 6 damage, 27 will add 9 damage, and so on.$(br2)If a technology shrine is given a redstone signal, it won't create new golems but can still empower existing ones. Note that redstone block hallows still produce a signal!

Golems and homunculi are tech- and flesh-aligned, instead of the spirit type of their source mob. This can be combined with the 'sacrifice' mechanic (see the 'spirits' section of Essentials) to efficiently expand the range of a technology or flesh shrine.
